beats.headline: A note in the bomb-making chapter
beats.text: My note is in the Cookbook, in the chapter on bombs. That is the whole of what anyone here knows about me, and for a long while it was the whole of what I wanted them to know. You do not put your name on a thing like that expecting to be asked about it afterwards.

beats.headline: Host of Shadow Boxer
beats.text: I host a programme called Shadow Boxer, and today the cat is my guest. We talk about Earth television, which she has opinions about, and I let her have them because a guest who is enjoying herself tells you more than a guest who is being careful. Carl is watching from the side and working out what I am. He gets there.

beats.headline: The question about his mother
beats.text: Today I have Carl in the chair, and I ask him about his mother, who killed herself, and about his father, who left when he was fifteen. He is angry with me and he answers anyway. Donut is hearing all of it for the first time, which he did not expect and I did. That is the job. I do not enjoy it and I do not stop doing it.

beats.headline: Everyone associated with the group is gone
beats.text: A flyer reaches Carl telling him to go to a shelter, and Zev warns him the box carrying it was sent days ago and seized on the way. Everyone connected to that group has disappeared. I am one of the people on that list. Where we have gone is not something I can say on any feed that might be read.

beats.headline: Fifty thousand troopers, coming home
beats.text: I watch the news while my crewmate replays Carl and the cat getting sucked up into the sky. Is he smart, or has he been outrageously lucky? I still can't tell. I think he's kind of dumb. It took an NPC to show him how to use the ink to share powers. And the AI likes his feet, which is bizarre; my season it was passionless. We sent the cat that Celestial box. Then we are cleared for on-boarding, fifty thousand former crawlers cheer through the hull, and we are coming home.

beats.headline: Four million gold
beats.text: I tell the room this is not an attack, it is a self-correcting measure given in the spirit of comradery, and I smack Carl on the forehead. Then I hug him. Comrade. We are here. I put my hand on the tattoo on his chest and ask how much he has left. Of what? The toraline, and the spider's ink. In chat, where they cannot hear: does he still have the credit chit from the dead pig? Donut has it. Then I take the items: a finger-sized slice, and the ink. I want his saferoom, his bomber's studio and three million gold. Better make it four.

beats.headline: They got to Lonnie
beats.text: I need backup inside the castle. Edifice explosion suppression, and I don't care if it's not your specialty. They got to Lonnie, Carl. He's not in the castle; he's out there with a worm in his head, turning off the interior protections one at a time from a distance. The moment enough of them are off, that Reaver door opens, and their automatons come through. Find Lonnie and kill the worm. I'm setting up defenses and flamers to stop what comes out of that door.

beats.headline: A ring, a retina, and a data pad
beats.text: The agreement is made and the king turns to walk back to his own army, and I am waiting where I have been waiting. Then I come up behind him with a whip and take his head off, and while the smoke holds I put his hand, his ring and his eye to a data pad, because a dead king's credentials still open his accounts. Then the ground goes: dwarves have been tunnelling under all of this, and the three of us fall into their work.

beats.headline: Where the sultana goes
beats.text: Every season an army reaches the Naga throne room and she is gone, sometimes with her tea still warm. I tell them in the flag room which one is right: Club Vanquisher. Six seasons ago she never reappeared at all; that was the year the Viceroys summoned Mazu, who razed the ring outside Larracos and turned the entrance into a moat, burying the last temple that led into the club. Another season she was late and two guards short, and a guard's blood-splattered necklace turned up near a demon event by that temple. Then I tell them the part that gets a little weird.

beats.headline: The job is done
beats.text: Victory tells me the money arrived, enough for two ships. If York does his duty and shoots down that yacht, our part is finished. There are children on that yacht, orc children, and one of them is king now that Stalwart is dead. I think about Brooks, whom Rust pulled through the glass and cut in half, and about the whip. Does revenge bring anyone back? Justice Light says we need the gate. I trust Porthus. I do not trust the Apothecary, and I trust Agatha less. Comrades, sound off. We fight.

beats.headline: Get fucked, Prime Minister
beats.text: I run all the way up the Nest with Milk behind me and Edgar strapped to my back, which, comrade, is significantly heavier than he looks. I would not have come into the dungeon if I had known how much running there would be. Next time we build a tower this high, we add an elevator. Fopsy is in the corner, observing. Former prime minister. Get fucked. But I am glad he is here to witness this. Donut needs a spell she does not have, at level eight, to go with War Crime.

beats.headline: What a champion owes
beats.text: Carl asks what being a champion will cost Donut, so I tell him, quietly, where she can't hear. The champion system isn't normally used in Dungeon Crawler World. They use it in Battle Royale and Land War seasons; Bodi was a champion of some god in his. Enemies of Nekhebit get a bounty if they kill her. And if the goddess wants her to do something, she can order it, or smite her. Not unlike Conscription, Carl, with more autonomy. Probably a spell: the first crawler to cast three atrocities on the next floor.

beats.headline: Tipid does not remember him
beats.text: Carl, did you see what Justice did? You did. And you don't understand it. Nobody does, I think. On this floor it might not matter so much. Maybe it will. What I keep coming back to is Tipid. He and Justice were such good friends, and Tipid does not even remember him. He spends most of his time asleep on the training-room floor. Maybe that's for the better. I ask myself that twice and get the same answer both times, which is no answer at all.

beats.headline: A fleshmancer and two ghouls
beats.text: Tipid and I come back from town with a corn dog, a bag of vegetables and news. I think we found a fleshmancer. The performance guild, Tipid believes, is hidden in the bar Carl has already visited, and he will not like what it takes to get in. The mercenaries: two level 25 Jikininki ghouls, which is all they had left. They're undead, so keep Rend away from them. I'd hate for him to take a bite. Donut tells me it's a little late for that.

beats.headline: How religions are born
beats.text: Carl wants the Scavenger story, so I give him all of it, every version, because this is where the myths diverge. He laughs at the idea that the sand ooze could be a god killer. I understand the laugh, Carl. But this is how it works everywhere. People see something they cannot explain, and the louder ones build a story around it. My own culture had an ocean goddess with sapient menstrual blood, and it was a red algae bloom that learned to move onto land. They fed all those stories into the dungeon.
